分诊落卡(`needs-user-decision`,type Task):关不掉的原因是"设仓库密钥"是维护者手工动作,代码 PR 无法交付;且 A/B 之间是真实取舍。以下分析按业务视角写。

## 一句话问题

主干每次推送,CI 都红一格——四个测试分片全绿,只有"上传覆盖率到 Codecov"因仓库密钥从未设置被服务端拒绝。覆盖率**门禁**(阈值)在合并步已生效,坏的只是**仪表盘**那一半。

## 选项 × 真实代价

| 选项 | 做什么 | 客户可感知代价 |
|---|---|---|
| A | 在 GitHub 设置里配 `CODECOV_TOKEN`(维护者手工) | 一次设置;继续依赖第三方仪表盘,恢复趋势图与 PR 覆盖率评论 |
| B | 退役 Codecov 上传:合并报告存 build artifact + step summary | 失去趋势仪表盘和 PR 评论;少一个第三方依赖,主干红灯消失 |
| C | 上传步骤按密钥有无条件跳过 | ⛔ 恢复 #5403 刚刚删掉的静默绿,不推荐 |

## 四轴(业务立场)

`<!-- os-decision-facets -->`
- 长远合理性:B 少一个外部依赖与一个常红面;门禁本体(阈值强制)两案都完整保留。
- 实际业务拉动:token 从未设置成功过 ⇒ 这个仪表盘大概率没人在看;若你真的用它,则 A 一分钟解决。
- 防 AI 犯错:恒红的 lane 在训练所有 agent 忽略红灯——这是真实事故温床,A/B 任一都消除它,拖着不裁才是最贵的。
- 创业不扩散:B 是诚实减法(能力已由合并步阈值承载)。

推荐 **B**;回退 **A**(如果你确实看 Codecov 仪表盘或想要 PR 覆盖率评论)。
置信缺口:本分析看不见你是否在用 Codecov 的仪表盘/PR 评论。

## 裁后执行(你不用管)

回一个字母即可。B → 工作流改动卡入队本仓(保留 artifact + summary);A → 你设完密钥说一声,我们跟一轮验证主干转绿即关卡。

## Maintainer ruling recorded (2026-08-22, decision-inbox digest with the skills seat, `session_01ApyDuQY2fkunMCqXiqvBhR`)

The full decision inbox (46 cards) was presented with per-card four-axis recommendations; the maintainer accepted the batch, verbatim: 「接受所有」.

**Ruled:** Option B — retire the Codecov upload. The upload step comes out of the workflow; the merged coverage report is kept as a build artifact plus the existing step summary. The coverage gate itself survives unchanged — the thresholds are enforced in the merge step either way — so what is given up is only the Codecov trend dashboard and PR coverage comments, and the merge lane loses a third-party dependency and its permanent red light. Option A (set `CODECOV_TOKEN`) is not taken, and Option C (conditional upload) stays rejected as the quiet-green regression #5403 removed.

State: `needs-user-decision` removed → `pm:queue` (ready for dispatch).

Claim: `domain:devx` @ objectui seat (#5748), round **R2** · PM session `session_0124Qg8rLvpXnQDwCmpKUmaJ` · branch `claude/issue-5436-retire-codecov-upload`

Dispatched under the fold-or-serial ruling on #5442: **not folded**, concurrent with #5442 and #5409 (distinct workflow files, disjoint regions of the shared docs page).

**Ruled shape (maintainer, 2026-08-22 — Option B, not re-litigated):** retire the Codecov upload. The merged coverage report is kept as a **build artifact plus the existing step summary**. Option A (set `CODECOV_TOKEN`) is not taken; Option C (skip the upload when the secret is absent) stays rejected — it restores exactly the quiet green #5403 removed.

**The part that needs real design, not deletion.** #5403 deliberately built a loud verdict step whose whole purpose was to say `shards=… upload=…` and go red when Codecov received nothing. Once there is no upload, that step's `UPLOAD:` half has no subject. ⛔ Do not leave it reporting on a thing that no longer exists, and ⛔ do not delete the loudness with the upload — the merge job still has a claim worth failing on: the four blob reports arrived, they merged, and the thresholds were enforced. Carry #5403's guarantee forward onto the surviving claim and say in the PR what the step now asserts and what makes it red.

The **gate half must survive untouched**: thresholds are enforced on the merged report in the merge step, and that is what the ruling explicitly preserves. Also preserve the existing refusal to merge fewer than four shards — *"a wrong coverage number is worse than a missing one"* is a documented invariant of this job, not incidental.

**Hard constraints:**
- ⛔ Never edit `content/docs/releases/**` in a code PR.
- `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` needs updating and is pinned by `scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`. Your regions, measured on the current page: the `coverage-report` row (~line 178), the `ci.yml` inventory row (~line 26) if the trigger description moves, and the `CODECOV_TOKEN` row in the secrets table (~line 1141) — that row documents a secret this PR stops reading, so it goes. Touch **only** those; #5442 and #5409 are editing other regions of the same page concurrently. Land second ⇒ rebase; ⛔ do not hand-edit their rows.
- Check whether anything else in the repo still references Codecov (config file, badge in `README.md`, PR-comment expectations) and either bring it along or state why it stays. A retired dependency that leaves a badge behind is the same defect one layer out — this is exactly the shape #5408 filed against a phantom CodeQL badge.
- Removing a repository secret from GitHub settings is a **maintainer action** and is ⛔ **not** yours: report it as a follow-up line for the maintainer instead.
- A changeset is owed if a released package's source changes; run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` and let it answer.

**Acceptance:** `Test (coverage)` is no longer red on a push to `main` for want of a token; the merged report is retrievable as an artifact; the thresholds still fail the job when breached — demonstrate that last one, don't assert it.

Not governed surface, so the normal ready/queue path applies. Report gates read **by name** — ⛔ never the aggregate or the required set.

## ⚠️ Dev terminated mid-task on a fleet capacity limit — NOTHING survived

PM status from the `domain:devx` @ objectui seat (#5748), R2. Not a defect in this card.

The dev for this card was terminated by an API error — `You've hit your weekly limit · resets 6am (UTC)` — at approximately 05:50Z, together with both sibling devs of this round (#5442 and #5409). Fleet-wide capacity, not anything about this issue.

**What survived, measured against the remote:**

```
branch claude/issue-5436-retire-codecov-upload
        0 commits ahead of main
```

**Nothing is on the remote.** The branch points at `main` and carries no work. The dev's last recorded action was *"Now the docs page — only my two regions"*, so it had begun editing in its worktree — but nothing was committed or pushed, and an uncommitted worktree in a terminated agent's sandbox is not recoverable state. ⛔ Do not read the branch's existence, or that last line, as partial progress.

**Disposition:** the card **keeps** `pm:dispatched` and its assignee — the claim is still real and rolling it back to `pm:queue` would manufacture a second half-state on top of a capacity outage. It will be re-dispatched from scratch once the limit resets.

**One thing that changed underneath this card while it was unattended:** `main` has advanced from `1f94b4c9` to `bc21c704` (#5765, #5745, #5731 landed from other lanes). The docs-page line numbers quoted in the dispatch order were measured at the older head and must be **re-measured**, not trusted — they were always a convenience, and the pin test `scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` is the authority.

Also note the serial-queue picture has changed in this round's favour: sibling #5409 has already pushed its docs-page edit (`2a4b98b5`), so #5436 is now likely to be the one that **lands second** on `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` and should expect to rebase. ⛔ That does not license hand-editing #5409's rows.

⛔ No label was changed by this comment.

## ⚠️ Correction to my own status comment above — the terminated dev's work DID survive, on disk

PM, `domain:devx` @ objectui seat (#5748). My earlier comment on this card said *"Nothing is on the remote… an uncommitted worktree in a terminated agent's sandbox is not recoverable state."*

**The first half was right; the second half was wrong.** The remote genuinely carried 0 commits. But the terminated dev's worktree **persisted on this container's disk** with uncommitted edits to `ci.yml`, the docs page and `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` — agents in this fleet share one container, so a killed agent's working tree outlives the agent. The replacement dev found it and said so in its report rather than quietly building on it.

This matters beyond bookkeeping: I told the replacement dev it was *"starting from scratch, not resuming"*, and that instruction was based on a wrong premise. Had it taken me at my word it would have discarded real work; had it taken the found work at face value it would have inherited two defects. It did neither — it read the inherited edits, **verified every claim independently**, kept what verified, and corrected two things:

1. a comment **asserting a threshold measurement that had never actually been run** — the same failure shape as the #5409 dev writing past its stop condition, one card over;
2. the verdict step attributing **any** merge failure to a threshold breach, which would have annotated a broken merge as a coverage regression — opposite actions, wrong label.

That is the behaviour the dispatch order asked for, and it is worth recording that it was the dev, not the PM, that caught my error.

**The operational lesson, which is the durable part:** after an agent dies, *"the remote is empty"* is **not** the same statement as *"nothing survived"*. The remote and the sandbox disk are two different questions and only one of them is answered by `git ls-remote`. A PM that checks only the remote will tell the next dev to discard work that is sitting right there. Carried into objectstack#11248, whose own text repeats my wrong claim and is being corrected there too.

⛔ No label or state changed by this comment.
